column1: # WARP-2498 — the heading-slug rule, stated once, checked by both sides.
# GitHub's algorithm turns a heading into the id an `#anchor` link targets:
# trim, lowercase, drop everything that is not a word character / whitespace /
# hyphen, then turn EACH whitespace character into one hyphen. That last word
# is load-bearing: "Track B — a cloud service" leaves two spaces where the em
# dash was, so the anchor is `b--a`, not `b-a`.
# TWO implementations depend on it, in two languages:
#   • `headingSlug()` — apps/web-dashboard/src/lib/integration-guides.ts, used
#     by the /help/integrations/<provider> route to give headings their ids;
#   • `slugify()` — scripts/check-setup-guides.sh, used to prove every
#     `#fragment` in the docs resolves to a heading that exists.
# If those two disagree, the checker passes links the browser cannot follow —
# which is exactly the failure WARP-2498 exists to close, one level up. So
# neither is trusted: both run this file and must produce the right-hand
# column. Add a case here when you meet a heading shape neither covers.
# Format: heading<TAB>expected-slug. Blank lines and #-comments are skipped.
# Leading/trailing whitespace cases are deliberately NOT expressed here —
# invisible in a TSV, and covered by the TypeScript unit test instead.
